lessons.title: Feeling Safe at Home
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe why home feels like a safe place.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what 'safe' means with examples.
lessons.main_activity: Children discuss what makes their home feel safe and cosy, drawing their favourite room.
key_questions: What makes you feel safe at home?
What is your favourite room?

differentiation.extension: Explain reasoning for favourite room in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note emotional security vocabulary — evidence for PSED.2.
lessons.plenary: Share favourite rooms with the group.
lessons.home_link: Talk about what makes your home feel cosy and safe.

lessons.title: Describing My Home
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe their home using at least two descriptive sentences.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult describes their own home as a model.
lessons.main_activity: Children describe their home (flat, house, rooms, garden) to a partner using full sentences.
key_questions: What rooms does your home have?
Do you have a garden or balcony?

differentiation.extension: Add extra descriptive detail unprompted

lessons.assessment_notes: Note sentence complexity — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Share one interesting fact learned about a partner's home.
lessons.home_link: Describe your home to a family member in detail.

lessons.title: Building Big with Large Blocks
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use whole-body movement to build and move large construction blocks safely.
lessons.starter_activity: Practise safe lifting technique (bend knees).
lessons.main_activity: Children work in small groups to build a large 'house' structure using big soft blocks, practising safe lifting and carrying.
key_questions: How do you lift safely?
How are you working together to build?

differentiation.extension: Plan the structure before building

lessons.assessment_notes: Note gross motor control and safety awareness — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Admire the built structures together.
lessons.home_link: Build a den or structure together at home with cushions/blankets.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'm'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 'm' and blend it into words (man, mat, map).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap s,a,t,p,i,n sounds.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'm' sound/action; blend new CVC words (man, mat, map, mad).
key_questions: What sound is this?
Can you blend m-a-t?

differentiation.extension: Write CVC words with 'm' independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'm' and blending.
lessons.plenary: Sing all 7 sounds learned so far.
lessons.home_link: Practise blending man, mat, map together.

lessons.title: Positional Language: Rooms in a House
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use positional language (on, in, under, next to) to describe object locations.
lessons.starter_activity: Hide a toy and describe its position for children to find it.
lessons.main_activity: Using a dolls house or floor plan, children place furniture/figures using positional instructions and describe locations to a partner.
resources_needed: Dolls house or floor plan mat
key_questions: Where is the chair?
Can you put the lamp on the table?

differentiation.extension: Use 4+ positional words including behind/between

lessons.assessment_notes: Note range of positional vocabulary used accurately — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Quick positional language quiz using classroom objects.
lessons.home_link: Play 'hide and describe' with a toy at home using positional words.

lessons.title: Types of Homes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name and describe different types of homes.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of different home types.
lessons.main_activity: Sort picture cards of homes into types (house, flat, bungalow); discuss which type of home each child lives in.
key_questions: What type of home do you live in?
How is a flat different from a house?

differentiation.extension: Sort into 4+ categories with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note vocabulary and categorisation skill — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Class tally of home types represented in the class.
lessons.home_link: Talk about what type of home you live in and why it suits your family.

lessons.title: Building a Junk Model House
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a simple house model by joining recycled materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at junk model house examples.
lessons.main_activity: Children build a house using recycled boxes, adding a roof and windows using craft materials.
key_questions: Where will the roof go?
How will you add windows?

differentiation.extension: Child plans and adds extra features (chimney, garden)

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe construction planning and material joining skill — evidence for EAD.1.
lessons.plenary: Display houses together as a 'model street'.
lessons.home_link: Build a house model together using recycling at home.

lessons.title: Tidying Up Together
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to take responsibility for tidying a shared space.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss why tidying up matters.
lessons.main_activity: Timed tidy-up challenge in the classroom, discussing everyone's role in keeping shared spaces nice.
key_questions: Why is it important to tidy up?
How did the class work together?

differentiation.support: Give a specific simple tidying job
differentiation.extension: Take initiative to help beyond assigned area

lessons.assessment_notes: Note responsibility and cooperation — evidence for PSED.2/PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate a tidy classroom together.
lessons.home_link: Help tidy a room at home this evening.

lessons.title: Listening for Household Sounds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify common household sounds by listening.
lessons.starter_activity: Guess a sound played on a recording/live demo (e.g. bell).
lessons.main_activity: Play a listening game identifying household sounds (doorbell, kettle boiling, vacuum) from audio or descriptions.
key_questions: What sound was that?
Where would you hear that sound at home?

differentiation.extension: Identify less common household sounds

lessons.assessment_notes: Note auditory discrimination and vocabulary — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of all household sounds identified.
lessons.home_link: Listen for and name household sounds this evening.

lessons.title: Home-Themed Cutting and Sticking
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to cut out shapes to represent furniture for a house collage.
lessons.starter_activity: Scissor warm-up practice.
lessons.main_activity: Children cut out pre-drawn furniture shapes and arrange/stick them into rooms on a large house outline.
key_questions: Which room does this furniture go in?
Can you cut along the line?

differentiation.extension: Cut more detailed/smaller shapes with precision

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe cutting control and precision — evidence for PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Display completed house collages.
lessons.home_link: Practise cutting simple shapes at home with supervision.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'The Three Little Pigs' (Homes Link)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare the three houses in the story and predict outcomes.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict which house will be strongest from the title/cover.
lessons.main_activity: Read 'The Three Little Pigs', pausing to discuss and predict which house material is strongest and why.
key_questions: Which house do you think will be strongest? Why?
What happened to the straw house?

differentiation.extension: Explain reasoning for material strength predictions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note prediction and reasoning skills — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap which material made the strongest house and why.
lessons.home_link: Retell the Three Little Pigs story to a family member.

lessons.title: Counting Windows and Doors
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count and compare quantities of windows/doors on different homes.
lessons.starter_activity: Count windows/doors visible in the classroom.
lessons.main_activity: Using picture cards of different homes, children count windows and doors on each, comparing which has more/fewer.
key_questions: How many windows does this house have?
Which house has more doors?

differentiation.extension: Count up to 10+ and compare multiple houses

lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting and comparing accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class tally of total windows counted across all pictures.
lessons.home_link: Count windows and doors at home together.

lessons.title: Rooms and Their Purposes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to match a room to its main purpose/activity.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what happens in the kitchen as an example.
lessons.main_activity: Match room name cards to activity picture cards (e.g. bedroom-sleeping, kitchen-cooking); discuss own home's room layout.
resources_needed: Room name and activity picture cards
key_questions: What do you do in this room?
Which room is your favourite and why?

differentiation.extension: Match 6+ rooms including less common ones (utility, study)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note vocabulary range for rooms/purposes — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of room-purpose matches.
lessons.home_link: Give your family a tour of your home naming each room's purpose.

lessons.title: Role-Play: Moving House
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to engage in imaginative role-play around a moving/home scenario.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what happens when a family moves house.
lessons.main_activity: Role-play packing boxes and 'moving' to a new home corner setup, using imaginative language about their new home.
key_questions: What are you packing?
What will your new home be like?

differentiation.support: Adult joins play to model language
differentiation.extension: Child narrates an imaginative story about the move

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative play and vocabulary use — evidence for EAD.2/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Share what everyone 'packed' for their pretend move.
lessons.home_link: Play a pretend packing/moving game at home.

lessons.title: Home Rules and Routines
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one rule or routine from their home.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss classroom rules learned in Week 1 as a comparison.
lessons.main_activity: Children share a rule/routine from home (bedtime, mealtime, screen time) and discuss why routines help us feel secure.
key_questions: What is a rule at your home?
Why do routines help us?

differentiation.extension: Explain the reasoning behind their home rule

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of routine/security — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Class list of different home routines shared.
lessons.home_link: Talk about your bedtime routine with your family.

lessons.title: Following Directions: My Way Home
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to follow simple directional instructions (left, right, straight).
lessons.starter_activity: Practise identifying left and right hand.
lessons.main_activity: Simple floor-map activity, following directional instructions to move a toy figure 'home' along a path.
key_questions: Which way do we turn now?
Are we going the right way home?

differentiation.extension: Use left/right/straight combined instructions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note directional language understanding — evidence for CL.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the journey taken to get 'home'.
lessons.home_link: Practise left and right while walking together.

lessons.title: Obstacle Course: Journey Home
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to navigate an obstacle course representing a journey home with control.
lessons.starter_activity: Warm-up stretches.
lessons.main_activity: Set up an obstacle course themed as 'the journey home' (crawl under a bridge, balance across a river, jump over a puddle) for children to complete.
key_questions: What obstacle is trickiest?
How do you stay balanced?

differentiation.extension: Add a timed or repeated challenge

lessons.assessment_notes: Note coordination and confidence — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Cool down; discuss the 'journey' completed.
lessons.home_link: Set up a simple obstacle course at home or in the garden.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'd'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 'd' and blend it into words (dad, din, mad).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all sounds learned so far.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'd' sound/action; blend new CVC words (dad, din, mad, dip).
key_questions: What sound is this?
Can you blend d-a-d?

differentiation.extension: Write CVC words with 'd' independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'd' and blending.
lessons.plenary: Sing all 8 sounds learned so far.
lessons.home_link: Practise blending dad, din, mad together.

lessons.title: Building Patterns with Bricks
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to continue and create a simple repeating pattern using building bricks.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a simple ABAB pattern example.
lessons.main_activity: Using two-colour building bricks, children continue given patterns and create their own repeating pattern 'wall'.
key_questions: What comes next in this pattern?
Can you make your own pattern?

differentiation.support: Continue simple ABAB pattern with support
differentiation.extension: Create own more complex pattern (ABBA, ABC)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note pattern recognition and creation — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Share and admire each other's pattern walls.
lessons.home_link: Look for and create patterns with objects at home.

lessons.title: What Are Homes Made Of?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name materials used to build homes and describe their properties.
lessons.starter_activity: Feel and compare brick, wood, and glass samples (safely).
lessons.main_activity: Explore material samples used in building homes, discussing which are strong/waterproof/see-through and why they're used.
resources_needed: Safe material samples (brick, wood, glass sample/picture)
key_questions: Which material is strongest?
Why do windows need to be see-through?

differentiation.extension: Compare 4+ materials and reason about suitability

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early scientific reasoning about material properties — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap why bricks are commonly used for building.
lessons.home_link: Look at what your home is made of and talk about it.

lessons.title: Brick Printing Pattern Art
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use a printing technique to create a brick-wall pattern.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a real brick wall pattern (photo or nearby wall).
lessons.main_activity: Children use sponge/block printing to create a repeating brick-wall pattern on paper.
key_questions: How are the bricks arranged?
Can you repeat your pattern?

differentiation.extension: Create an accurate offset brick pattern

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe pattern replication skill — evidence for EAD.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Display brick pattern artwork together.
lessons.home_link: Look for brick or tile patterns around your home/neighbourhood.

lessons.title: Welcoming a Visitor Home
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to demonstrate polite welcoming behaviour in a role-play scenario.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how we welcome a guest politely.
lessons.main_activity: Role-play welcoming a 'guest' (puppet or partner) into a pretend home, practising polite phrases and turn-taking.
key_questions: How do we welcome a guest politely?
What could you say when they arrive?

differentiation.support: Adult models the polite phrases to repeat
differentiation.extension: Child extends the scenario with own ideas

lessons.assessment_notes: Note social skills and politeness — evidence for PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap polite welcoming phrases learned.
lessons.home_link: Practise welcoming a guest politely at home.

lessons.title: Explaining Why Homes Need Certain Rooms
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why a room is needed using 'because'.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models an explanation: 'We need a kitchen because we cook food there.'
lessons.main_activity: Children explain why 2-3 rooms are needed using the 'because' sentence structure, supported by picture prompts.
key_questions: Why do we need a bathroom?
Why do we need a bedroom?

differentiation.support: Adult provides sentence frame to complete
differentiation.extension: Explain 4+ rooms independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note use of causal language ('because') — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of room explanations.
lessons.home_link: Explain why your family needs your home's rooms.

lessons.title: Fine Motor: Building Small World Homes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to manipulate small construction pieces with precision.
lessons.starter_activity: Finger warm-up exercises.
lessons.main_activity: Children use small-world building bricks/Lego to construct a miniature house, requiring careful fitting and placement.
key_questions: How do these pieces fit together?
What did you build?

differentiation.extension: Use smaller Lego bricks for finer precision

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor precision and problem-solving — evidence for PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Display and describe small-world houses built.
lessons.home_link: Build a small-world model at home with any building toys available.

lessons.title: Writing a 'For Sale' Sign for a Home
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write simple words/phrases for a role-play purpose.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at an example estate agent sign/leaflet.
lessons.main_activity: Children design and write a simple 'For Sale' sign for their junk-model house from Monday, using known phonics sounds.
key_questions: What words will you write on your sign?
What sound does that word start with?

differentiation.extension: Child attempts independent phonetic writing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note purposeful writing attempt — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Set up a pretend 'estate agent' display with all signs and houses.
lessons.home_link: Make a sign for a pretend shop or den at home.

lessons.title: Ordering House Numbers
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to order numerals 1-10 as if they were house numbers on a street.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap numeral recognition 1-10.
lessons.main_activity: Children arrange numeral cards (1-10) in order as 'house numbers' along a pretend street floor line.
key_questions: Which number comes next on the street?
What number is missing?

differentiation.extension: Order numerals 1-10 and identify missing numbers in a sequence

lessons.assessment_notes: Record numeral ordering ability — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Walk along the 'street' counting the house numbers in order.
lessons.home_link: Look at house/door numbers on your street and talk about their order.

lessons.title: Homes for Animals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to match animals to their natural homes.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss where a bird lives (nest) as an example.
lessons.main_activity: Match animal picture cards to their home type (nest, den, burrow, hive, web) and discuss why each home suits the animal.
key_questions: Where does this animal live?
Why is that a good home for it?

differentiation.extension: Match 6+ pairs and explain reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of habitats — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of animal homes matched.
lessons.home_link: Look for animal homes (nests, burrows) on a walk together.

lessons.title: Decorating a Room Diorama
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use materials to decorate a small 3D room space purposefully.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a completed room diorama example.
lessons.main_activity: Using a shoebox, children design and decorate a miniature room with furniture cut-outs and craft materials.
key_questions: What room have you made?
What furniture did you add?

differentiation.extension: Design and cut own furniture shapes, add wallpaper/flooring detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe design choices and material use — evidence for EAD.1.
lessons.plenary: Display room dioramas as a class 'dolls house street'.
lessons.home_link: Continue decorating the diorama at home if taken home, or design a new room.

lessons.title: My Home Is Special: Reflection
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to express one reason their home is special to them.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about homes.
lessons.main_activity: Children complete 'My home is special because ___' and share with the group, celebrating the diversity of homes in the class.
key_questions: What makes your home special?
What did you learn about homes this week?

differentiation.extension: Give 2-3 reasons with elaboration

lessons.assessment_notes: Note reflective and expressive language — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Class cheer celebrating everybody's special homes.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family why your home is special to you.

lessons.title: Homes Quiz Game
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer questions about homes learned this week, demonstrating listening and recall.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap key vocabulary from the week with actions/props.
lessons.main_activity: Quiz-style game: adult asks questions about homes (rooms, materials, animal homes) and children answer using recall from the week.
key_questions: What room do we cook in?
What is a bird's home called?

differentiation.extension: Open questions without prompts

lessons.assessment_notes: Assess recall and listening comprehension — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.plenary: Team points tally, celebrate together.
lessons.home_link: Quiz a family member on what you learned about homes this week.

lessons.title: Whole-Body Review: Building and Moving Challenge
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to combine balance, coordination, and lifting skills in a review challenge.
lessons.starter_activity: Warm-up stretches recapping the week's PD vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Combined challenge: lift and carry soft blocks to build a small structure, then balance-walk around it.
key_questions: Which part was trickiest?
How did you stay balanced/safe lifting?

differentiation.extension: Add a timed element or extra obstacle

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 4 PD progress — evidence for PD.1/PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Cool down and celebrate completing the challenge.
lessons.home_link: Build and balance around a structure at home/garden.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: s,a,t,p,i,n,m,d
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read CVC words using all 8 sounds learned so far.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick-fire flashcard review of all 8 sounds.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations: word-building with magnetic letters, CVC word reading cards, sound-writing practice, simple sentence reading (e.g. 'a mat').
key_questions: Can you build and read this word?
Can you read this short sentence?

differentiation.extension: Read simple phrases/sentences independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Finalise week 4 phonics tracker for all 8 sounds and reading ability.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all sounds learned with a phonics song and reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading simple words/phrases together over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Position, Pattern, and Number
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply positional language, pattern-making, and number ordering skills learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's key maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: positional language with dolls house, pattern building with bricks, ordering house numbers.
key_questions: Where is this object?
What comes next in the pattern?
What number is this?

differentiation.extension: Independent completion with recording

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 4 maths observations for each child.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining position, pattern, and number.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising patterns and counting together over the weekend.

lessons.title: Homes Recap: Materials and Purpose
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise what makes a good home using ideas learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the Three Little Pigs and material strength discussion.
lessons.main_activity: Class discussion synthesising the week's learning: what makes a home strong, safe, and comfortable; children vote on the best material for building.
resources_needed: Material samples from earlier in the week
key_questions: What makes a good home?
Which material would you choose to build with and why?

differentiation.support: Choose from 2 given options with reasoning support
differentiation.extension: Give a full reasoned explanation independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's scientific/geographic learning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Class vote and discussion on best building material.
lessons.home_link: Discuss what makes your home strong, safe and comfortable.

lessons.title: My Dream Home: Imaginative Drawing and Talk
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to imagine and describe a 'dream home' creatively.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss: 'If you could have any home, what would it be like?'
lessons.main_activity: Children draw and describe an imaginative 'dream home' (e.g. treehouse, castle, home on the moon), sharing their ideas with the group.
key_questions: What is special about your dream home?
Who would live there with you?

differentiation.extension: Describe dream home in detailed sentences

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative thinking and expressive language — evidence for EAD.2/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Class gallery walk admiring everyone's dream homes.
lessons.home_link: Describe your dream home to your family this weekend.
